scope: Independent reading of retained static projection blocks only; no linked appendices, image equations, omitted policy blockquotes or measurement sources.

findings.assessment: Combined standard uncertainty is an estimated standard deviation obtained from individual standard uncertainties and covariances as appropriate, with Type A and Type B contributions.
findings.limit: The prose does not authorize ignoring covariance or provide the unacquired Appendix A equation. This measurement-propagation statement is distinct from assumptions of a joint-risk theorem.

findings.assessment: The account assumes compensation for recognized significant systematic effects and treats uncertainty of an applied correction separately from systematic error. A note acknowledges impractical correction in some limited-resource cases while urging conformity as far as possible.
findings.limit: An uncorrected effect is not automatically the same quantity as correction uncertainty; neither this guidance nor a documentary No field alone establishes the magnitude/significance of a particular BAM effect or invalidates its reported budget.

findings.assessment: The approximate one-standard-uncertainty coverage statement requires an approximately normal characterized distribution and negligible uncertainty in the combined standard uncertainty. NIST describes a common CLT-based case with many well-behaved contributions of comparable importance and adequate linear approximation.
findings.limit: These premises have not been verified for BAM by this reading. The CLT example is not a proof that every reported k=2 result is normal, nor a claim that this is the only route to normality.

findings.assessment: Confidence interval has a specific statistical meaning requiring conditions including Type A evaluation of every contributing component. The guideline instead describes coverage probability of the distribution characterized by the result and its combined uncertainty.
findings.limit: Including is not if-and-only-if; all Type A components alone are not stated sufficient. Metrological coverage wording does not automatically establish a frequentist repeated-sampling, conditional, posterior or simultaneous-coverage interpretation.

findings.assessment: Expanded uncertainty is defined as the coverage factor times combined standard uncertainty; the cautions of5.5 also apply to that expanded interval.
findings.limit: This definitional relation does not, by algebra alone, identify an exact physical error standard deviation, error distribution or coverage guarantee for a separate data source.

findings.assessment: The k=2 approximate95percent statement explicitly requires the normal distribution and negligible uncertainty in the combined standard uncertainty.
findings.limit: Approximate is not exact, scalar coverage is not simultaneous coverage, and no premise is transferred to BAM or Lupine without justification.

findings.assessment: Assigning a specific coverage level to k is difficult in practice; it requires detailed probability distributions for the quantities on which the measurand depends and their combination into the measurand distribution.
findings.limit: A numerical coverage factor alone does not determine that distribution or joint endpoint risk.

omissions: Direct policy blockquotes introduced in5.3,6.5,6.6 are not part of the bounded text projection, and image equations were not extracted. No content of those missing blocks, unrequested Appendix A/B/C or linked works is supplied here.
scientific_implication: Guidance supports keeping measurement definitions and coverage assumptions explicit. It does not establish BAM per-test budgets, Z convention, dependence, a latent-property model, sampling/exchangeability or future-prediction validity. Existing BAM evidence was not reread.
publication: Own paraphrase and locators only; no full projection, public-contact roster or raw HTML copied.
